findings: GetShardCostList allocates a List<BreakInfinity.BigDouble> and then appends shard costs by calling the per-row get_SU*Cost getter family in order.
That means the shared cost-list path does not replace the row getters with a separate hidden formula; it materializes the same getter outputs into MilestoneCostList.
UpdateShardCostList refreshes the owner-side MilestoneCostList field before downstream sorting and affordability work.
SortCostAndBools calls GetShardCostList and combines the resulting costs with owned-state booleans into a separate sorted list.
CountAffordableShard folds the sorted cost list against the current shard currency lane, so affordability is downstream of the getter family rather than an alternate cost computation path.
currentBoundary: Treat GetShardCostList as a checked owner-side cache builder for the same per-row getter outputs, not as proof of a different shard cost formula.
Treat UpdateShardCostList, SortCostAndBools, and CountAffordableShard as downstream consumers of the getter family.
Do not expose exact shard next-costs until the repo still proves how each get_SU*Cost getter itself assembles the returned BreakInfinity.BigDouble.
